question.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Polygon Under an Affine Transformation
question.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/838861910879e95b0e1c3055da9f9597f194950c3823867a20a1e3c149354437.png)

Consider the rectangle $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ=\{(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 2\}.
$$

The transformation $T$ is defined as

$$
x=2u-v+1,\,y=u-v+1.
$$

Which of the following gives the image of $Δ$ in the $xy$-plane under the action of $T?$
question.worked_solution:
An affine transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ is a function of the form

$$
x=Au+b,
$$

where $x,u,$ and $b$ are column vectors in ${R}^{2},$ and $A$ is a $2\times 2$ matrix.

Notice that we can express the given transformation as

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}2u-v+1 \\ u-v+1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2u-v \\ u-v\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & ={{[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{A}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}u \\ v\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{u}+{{[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{b}\end{aligned}
$$

The transformation $T$ maps the boundary of $Δ$ to the boundary of the image. So, to find the image of $Δ,$ we find the images of each side.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/c89be48140d49ce8c9def44122aa2bfac779bdd02cfbfbe98f97d414a5637409.png)

          

To quickly carry out this calculation, we set up the following matrices:

- The matrix $U$ containing all vertices of our square:

$$
U=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$

- The matrix $B$ that has the same shape as $U$ and with the vector $b$ in each column:

$$
B=[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

The image of $u$ under $T$ is given by $Au+b.$ So, by applying $T$ to $U,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}AU+B & =[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 \\ 1 & -1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 2 & 0 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & -2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & 1 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 3 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 2 & 0 & -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the vertices of the image in the $xy$-plane are $(1,1),(3,2),(1,0),$ and $(-1,-1).$

Drawing this region in the $xy$-plane, we get the following: 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14095879/assets/d038caec0aa360e5d8cc1bcb4a3aa4d88408496d947b312d47634e51bbf4a11f.png)

          

Finally, since $det(A)=-1<0,$ this transformation is not orientation-preserving.

judgment.reasoning: All five answers agree with their own captured Math Academy worked solutions. For a sin(x)+b cos(x), coefficient matching and sin²(phi)+cos²(phi)=1 give the positive amplitude R=sqrt(a²+b²), regardless of the stated sine or cosine phase form. Thus q-80131 gives sqrt(16+1)=sqrt(17), q-80126 gives sqrt(7+9)=4, and q-11295 gives sqrt(4+9)=sqrt(13). For q-124641, applying T to (0,0),(1,0),(1,2),(0,2) gives (1,1),(3,2),(1,0),(-1,-1), matching option 2. Its worked solution incorrectly calls the original rectangle a square, but the vertices and image calculation are correct. For q-124343, T(u,v)=(1-v,1+u) maps (0,1),(2,1),(2,2) to (0,1),(0,3),(-1,3), matching option 0. These two image answers agree with the earlier review. No submission grade is supplied; MA answer evidence comes from the captured worked solutions.
